title: The gene-regulatory evolution of the human skeleton.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found two GEO series (gene expression archive entries) by title search, as PubMed elink returned none: GSE316891 (MPRA, massively parallel reporter assay, 70 samples) and GSE316892 (hybrid-cell RNA-seq, 10 samples). Read the GSE316891 filelist: only ten FASTA oligo libraries (~8 MB each) and ten oligo-to-barcode maps (117-379 MB each, over the cap and not downloaded); the 60 DNA/RNA count samples have supplementary_file = NONE. Downloaded GSM9462019_L1a1.fasta.gz: 79,812 sequences of 270 bp, headers like seq_41884_chr1:1211358-1211627_SCREEN_ancestral_a1_L1 (GRCh37 coordinates, human/ancestral allele tag). Downloaded GSE316892 read-count TSV: 40,344 genes x 10 hybrid samples, allele-specific counts (human, chimp/gorilla, no-ASE (allele-specific expression), ambiguous).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 561,410 substitutions assayed and 15,077 loci with human-specific activity (abstract; the GEO summary says 574,290). The GEO processing note promises an activity_and_differential_activity.txt file with per-oligo activity and allele logFC (log fold change) plus FDR (false discovery rate); I could not find it anywhere in GEO. Full text and supplementary tables are paywalled (no PMCID), so I could not check whether Nature's supplement contains that table.

a1_downloadable.note: GEO is open; I downloaded files from both series. The per-oligo results table described in GEO was not deposited (checked filelist.txt).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked in files: no deposited table gives per-oligo MPRA activity or human-versus-ancestral difference. The label would have to be rebuilt from raw SRA (sequence read archive) barcode reads plus 2.3 GB of barcode maps.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked: the oligo FASTA files hold the 270 bp human and ancestral sequences themselves, roughly 80k per sub-library.

a4_units_stated.note: There is no label column, so no units. The undeposited file would hold log fold change and FDR (from the GEO text only).

a5_enough_rows.note: 79,812 sequences counted in 1 of 10 sub-libraries. The other nine are similar in file size, implying ~800k oligos, but I counted only one.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~2.5 GB of barcode maps plus raw SRA reads for 60 DNA/RNA libraries
a6_fits_laptop.note: Rebuilding the label means processing raw sequencing reads, which the project rules forbid and which is far beyond the working set.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The abstract says 561,410 substitutions; the GEO summary says 574,290. The deposited files can't settle it because no results table exists.

a8_label_provenance.note: In principle the label is a physical measurement: RNA/DNA barcode ratios in fetal chondrocytes (cartilage cells). It is not a model output, but it isn't deposited.

existing_models.name: Whalen et al. 2023 (Neuron), machine learning on HAR (human accelerated region) MPRAs in neural progenitors, using Sei and other models
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved in detail; search snippet only.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Snippet notes compensatory variants with opposite effects inside the same HAR.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome or Enformer-style DNA sequence model (variant effect from 270 bp oligos)
backbone.hardware: CPU feasible for embedding 270 bp oligos, but moot without labels

integration.partner_dataset: Hybrid-cell allele-specific expression (GSE316892) on gene symbol; GTEx (tissue expression atlas)
integration.join_key: GRCh37 coordinates to nearest gene symbol
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequence-predicted MPRA effects of human-derived substitutions explain human-versus-ape allele-specific expression in skeletal progenitor cells?

controls.positive_control: Would be: known strong promoters among oligos should show high activity; GC content as a trivially learnable target.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the labels within each sub-library.
controls.external_validation: The GBE 2026 human-versus-chimp postcranial skeleton MPRA (70k regions) could serve as an external set; not downloaded.

honest_claim_h3: If the labels existed: the model predicts how a human-derived substitution changes reporter activity in cultured fetal chondrocytes, outside its native chromatin, for ~270 bp windows.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the human and ancestral versions of short regulatory DNA pieces to predict whether each human mutation changes gene activity in cartilage cells.
plain_idea.train_on: 270-letter DNA sequences in human and ancestral-ape versions; roughly 800k oligos estimated, 79,812 counted in one of ten libraries.
plain_idea.predict: How much each sequence turns on a reporter gene in fetal chondrocytes, and the human-versus-ancestral difference, measured by RNA-to-DNA barcode counts. Those values are not deposited.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Evolutionary and skeletal-disease geneticists could rank human-specific mutations without running new assays, and could test whether sequence models trained on other cells carry over to cartilage.

ml_idea: Fit a frozen DNA-model embedding plus a head to predict allele effects on MPRA activity in chondrocytes, and test how well it transfers from neuronal HAR MPRAs. This is blocked until the per-oligo activity table is found.

effort.compute_note: Estimated only. Rebuilding labels needs raw SRA barcode reads plus 2.3 GB of barcode maps, which is out of scope.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open Nature's Supplementary Tables (manual download by the user) and check for a per-oligo table with sequence ID, activity, allele logFC and FDR. If it's absent, the project is dead.

verdict_reason: Fails A2: GEO holds oligo sequences and barcode maps but no per-oligo activity or allele-effect table, even though GEO's own processing note describes one. Rebuilding the label needs raw sequencing reads. It could revive if Nature's supplement, which I couldn't check, contains that table.
